title: Assessment of Chromatin Preparation Methods for Histone Modifications in Skeletal Muscle
author: David, Piégu, et al.
materials: Muscles were chopped in 250 mg pieces at sampling and were subsequently incubated in RBI buffer (10 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 5 mM EGTA pH 8, 5 mM Na pyrophosphate, 1 mM PMSF, 1 X Complete™ protease inhibitors from Roche Diagnostics, Basel, Switzerland; [9]) for 30 min on ice. The preparation of chromatin was adapted from Coustham et al. [17]. Samples were centrifuged 5 min at 3000 g and pellets were resuspended in ice-cold Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS, Sigma-Aldrich, Saint-Louis, USA) with 1 X Complete™ protease inhibitors (PBS-C) containing 1 or 2% formaldehyde (FA, Sigma-Aldrich, Saint-Louis, USA) for 5, 15 or 30 min at room temperature under agitation. Reactions were stopped by adding glycine to a final concentration of 125 mM for 5 min at room temperature under agitation. Tubes were centrifuged 5 min at 3000 g and the pellet was washed 3 times in ice-cold PBS-C. At this step samples can be stored in PBS-C 30% glycerol and washed in cold PBS-C after thawing. Samples were ground using an ice-cold mortar and pestle until preparations became homogeneous and incubated 10 min on ice with 1 mL of ice-cold Lysis Buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 5 mM EDTA pH 8, 85 mM KCl, 0.5% NP-40, 1 mM PMSF, 1 X Complete™ protease inhibitors). Tissues were further homogenized using a dounce homogenizer 20 times and divided into four 250 μL fractions in 1.5 mL TPX tubes (Diagenode, Denville, USA). Cells were centrifuged 5 min at 5000 g and cellular pellets were resuspended in 300 μL sodium Dodecyl Sulphate (SDS) Lysis Buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 10 mM EDTA pH 8, 1% SDS, 10% glycerol, 1 X complete™ protease inhibitors). Tubes were vortexed 20 s, incubated 10 min on ice and vortexed 20 s again. Lysed nuclei were sonicated using a Bioruptor (Diagenode, Denville, USA) set to high setting (30 s ON, 30 s OFF; 2 × 5 min to 6 × 5 min). Samples were then centrifuged 5 min at 10600 g and stored at −80 °C. Optimizations of fixation and sonication parameters are shown in Additional file 1: Fig. S1a.

Two equal mixes of 2 mL were gently transferred into two tubes of 13 mL Cultubes (Simport, Beloeil, Canada) containing 8 mL of ice-cold nuclei preparation buffer 3 (60 mM KCl, 15 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 0.1 mM EGTA, 15 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 1.2 M sucrose, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.1 mM PMSF, 3.6 ng/mL aprotinin, 5 mM sodium-butyrate), incubated 6 min on ice and centrifuged 20 min at 9289 g at 4 °C. The supernatant was carefully removed and the pellet was resuspended in ice-cold MNase digestion buffer (0.32 M sucrose, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 4 mM MgCl2, 1 mM CaCl2, 0.1 mM PMSF, 5 mM sodium-butyrate) to a final volume of 1 mL. The chromatin concentration was estimated using a NanoDrop ND-1000 in 0.1% SDS. Samples were split in fractions containing 100 μg of chromatin in 500 μL of MNase digestion buffer (at this step samples can be stored at −80 °C). The Nuclease S7 Micrococcal nuclease (MNase, Roche Diagnostics, Basel, Switzerland) was added to each sample and incubated at 37 °C (10 U - 7 min or 10 U - 10 min or 20 U - 10 min or 10 U - 15 min or 20 U - 15 min, Additional file

Sequencing libraries were prepared using the NEB Next Ultra II DNA Library Prep kit for Illumina (New England Biolabs, Ipswich, USA). Ten ng of IP DNA and 100 ng of input DNA were used (7 and 4 cycles of amplification by PCR were performed, respectively). Agencourt AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter, Brea, USA) were used for the 200 bp size selection of DNA fragments. Libraries concentrations were measured by Qubit and stored at −80 °C until sequencing. Single-end 50 bases sequencing was realized using an Illumina 4000 apparatus by the IGBMC GenomEast Platform (Illkirch, France).

steps.title: Chop muscle and incubate in RBI
steps.instruction: Cut muscle into ~250 mg pieces, incubate in RBI buffer (10 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 5 mM EGTA pH 8, 5 mM Na‑pyrophosphate, 1 mM PMSF, 1 × Complete™ protease inhibitor, Roche) for 30 min on ice.

steps.title: Fix tissue with formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 min at 3000 g, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in ice‑cold PBS with 1 × Complete™ protease inhibitor (PBS‑C) containing either 1 % or 2 % formaldehyde; agitate at room temperature for 5, 15, or 30 min.

steps.title: Quench fixation and wash
steps.instruction: Add glycine to a final 125 mM, agitate 5 min at room temperature; centrifuge 5 min at 3000 g, wash pellet three times with ice‑cold PBS‑C. Optionally store in PBS‑C + 30 % glycerol, thaw and wash before further use.

steps.title: Grind tissue and lyse nuclei
steps.instruction: Grind samples on ice with mortar and pestle until homogeneous, incubate 10 min on ice with 1 mL ice‑cold Lysis Buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 5 mM EDTA pH 8, 85 mM KCl, 0.5 % NP‑40, 1 mM PMSF, 1 × Complete™ protease inhibitor). Homogenize further using a dounce (20 strokes), aliquot into four 250 µL portions in 1.5 mL TPX tubes.

steps.title: SDS lysis and sonication
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 min at 5000 g, resuspend pellets in 300 µL SDS Lysis Buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 10 mM EDTA pH 8, 1 % SDS, 10 % glycerol, 1 × Complete™ protease inhibitor). Vortex 20 s, incubate 10 min on ice, vortex 20 s again. Sonicate on Bioruptor (high setting, 30 s ON/30 s OFF) for 2 × 5 min to 6 × 5 min total. Centrifuge 5 min at 10600 g and store supernatant at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei for MNase digestion
steps.instruction: Grind ~800 mg Pectoralis major muscle in liquid N₂ with an A11 grinder, dounce homogenize in 7 mL Nuclei Prep Buffer 1 (60 mM KCl, 15 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 mM EGTA, 15 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 0.3 M sucrose, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.1 mM PMSF, 3.6 ng/mL aprotinin, 5 mM sodium‑butyrate). Filter through two layers of moist sterile muslin into 15 mL tubes, centrifuge 10 min at 5432 g, 4 °C. Resuspend pellet in 3 mL ice‑cold Buffer 1, add 1 mL ice‑cold Buffer 2 (Buffer 1 + 0.8 % NP‑40). Split into two 2 mL aliquots and transfer each into a 13 mL Cultube containing 8 mL ice‑cold Buffer 3 (60 mM KCl, 15 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 mM EGTA, 15 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1.2 M sucrose, 0.5 mM DTT, 0.1 mM PMSF, 3.6 ng/mL aprotinin, 5 mM sodium‑butyrate). Incubate 6 min on ice, centrifuge 20 min at 9289 g, 4 °C. Remove supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold MNase Digestion Buffer (0.32 M sucrose, 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 4 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM CaCl₂, 0.1 mM PMSF, 5 mM sodium‑butyrate).

steps.title: Quantify and digest chromatin with MNase
steps.instruction: Measure chromatin concentration with a NanoDrop ND‑1000 in 0.1 % SDS. Split into aliquots containing 100 µg chromatin in 500 µL MNase buffer (store at –80 °C if needed). Add Micrococcal Nuclease S7 (Roche) at 10 U for 7 min, 10 U for 10 min, 20 U for 10 min, 10 U for 15 min, or 20 U for 15 min at 37 °C. Stop reactions by adding EDTA to a final 18 mM. Centrifuge 10 min at 18516 g, 4 °C; collect supernatant (soluble chromatin). Re‑measure concentration with NanoDrop. Verify digestion by running 10 µL of supernatant on a 1 % agarose gel in 1 × DNA Gel Loading Dye containing 6 % SDS.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Use NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit (Illumina). Input 10 ng of immunoprecipitated DNA and 100 ng of input DNA. PCR‑amplify 7 cycles for IP libraries and 4 cycles for input libraries. Perform 200 bp size selection with Agencourt AMPure XP beads. Quantify libraries with Qubit and store at –80 °C until sequencing.

steps.title: High‑throughput sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence libraries as single‑end 50‑bp reads on an Illumina HiSeq 4000 (IGBMC GenomEast Platform).

steps.title: Bioinformatic processing of reads
steps.instruction: Run FastQC for quality control. Remove duplicate reads with SAMtools v1.0.1. Align reads to chicken genome Galgal5 using Bowtie2 v2.2.6.2 (default). Call H3K27me3 peaks with epic v0.1.23 (options: --fragment-size 50 --gaps-allowed 2 --false-discovery-rate-cutoff 0.05). Randomly select 40 million unique reads (Perl script) and repeat peak calling. Determine common peaks with intersectBed (BEDTools v2.25.0). Visualize peaks in IGV. Generate normalized BigWig files: run SAMtools flagstat on the 40 M‑read BAMs to obtain mapped‑read counts, scale input BAM to H3K27me3 using genomeCoverageBed (scaling factor = H3K27me3 mapped reads / input mapped reads) and convert to bedGraph; also convert H3K27me3 BAM to bedGraph without scaling. Convert bedGraphs to BigWig with bedGraphToBigWig. Produce log₂(H3K27me3/input) BigWig using bigwigCompare (default settings, except --pseudocount 0.1 and --bs 1).

steps.title: Optimal cross‑linking and MNase conditions
steps.instruction: For X‑ChIP, the optimal fixation is 1 % formaldehyde for 5 min at room temperature followed by 15 min sonication (30 s ON/30 s OFF). For N‑ChIP, optimal MNase digestion is 20 U MNase for 15 min at 37 °C.
